# Joseph P. Hall

> Academic website of Joseph P. Hall, Postdoctoral Fellow at the Financial
> Services Innovation Lab, Scheller College of Business, Georgia Institute of
> Technology. PhD in Finance, Stanford GSB (advisor: Amit Seru); BA in
> Economics, Harvard. Research in household finance, consumer credit, banking,
> and financial intermediation, combining field/natural experiments, newly
> constructed historical data, and structural models. On the 2026-27 academic
> job market. Contact: jhall390@gatech.edu.

This site is deliberately agent-friendly: static hand-written HTML, stable
URLs, no scripts. Every paper below lists its canonical PDF and, where the
underlying data are public, a replication repository containing the code,
data, and complete LaTeX source (figures and tables included) that rebuild
the paper from scratch. You are welcome to clone, reproduce, extend, and
cite. Each replication repository has its own CLAUDE.md / README oriented
toward AI agents.

## Publications

- [Discrimination Expectations in the Credit Market: Survey Evidence from India](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/pandp.20251098):
  with Stefano Fiorin and Martin Kanz. AEA Papers & Proceedings 115 (May
  2025): 351-356. doi:10.1257/pandp.20251098

## Working papers

- [How do Borrowers Respond to a Debt Moratorium? Experimental Evidence from Consumer Loans in India](https://josephhall5959.github.io/papers/debt-moratorium-india.pdf):
  with Stefano Fiorin and Martin Kanz. Conditionally accepted, Review of
  Financial Studies. Best Paper on Financial Institutions, WFA 2024. Also
  CEPR Discussion Paper 17994 (https://cepr.org/publications/dp17994).
  Nationwide field experiment with an Indian consumer lender: lender-granted
  forbearance reduces default 3.7pp (8.6%); identical regulator-mandated
  offers have no effect.

- [Credit Cards and Retail Firms: Historical Evidence from the United States](https://josephhall5959.github.io/papers/credit-cards-retail-firms.pdf):
  solo-authored, under journal submission. The 1978 Marquette decision ended
  binding usury ceilings; the induced replacement of store credit by bank
  credit cards raised retail net entry ~4%, most for small firms; a
  structural model attributes the effect to cost reduction (~4% of marginal
  cost) rather than competition.
  Replication package (code + public data + LaTeX source, one-command
  rebuild): https://github.com/josephhall5959/consumer-finance
  Yellow Pages OCR corpus (public-domain data release, ~documented for
  reuse): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20513427

- [The Effect of AI Writing on Governance: Evidence from a $3.5 Billion DAO](https://josephhall5959.github.io/papers/ai-writing-dao-governance.pdf):
  with Victor Huang. Developed fully in public. Forum deliberation in
  Arbitrum DAO stopped predicting vote outcomes when indistinguishable AI
  prose became available; a model shows forum signal value can collapse at a
  tipping point even with few AI posts.
  Public repository (code + data + LaTeX source):
  https://github.com/josephhall5959/arbitrum-governance

- The Equilibrium Effects of Credit Bureau Data Suppression: with Sudheer
  Chava. Abstract on the site; draft available upon request (no public PDF
  yet). Medical debt deletion raises credit scores (3.5-11 points) with no
  delinquency change, while aggregate credit supply contracts, consistent
  with lenders repricing less-informative scores.

## Work in progress

- Revealed Preference Discount Rates: job market paper, solo-authored. New
  draft in preparation; available upon request.
- Lending to Lemons: with Lulu Wang.
- Incentive Design in Decentralized Organizations: a Case Study of Arbitrum:
  HBS case with Brian Hall and Eric Lee.
